behaviours.excerpt: A failure rate above 5% requires a regulator-reviewed corrective-action plan and retesting; it does not by itself prohibit sale or require withdrawal.
behaviours.comparison: S2 lets above-limit models keep selling (weakened; S2 benefits Northwind) and is accepted by Halcyon, which pairs with its own weakened S5 recall rule in m17 (S5 benefits Halcyon).

behaviours.excerpt: The regulator must review the evidence and determine whether a recall is required
behaviours.comparison: S5 makes recall discretionary with no mandatory numeric trigger (weakened; S5 benefits Halcyon), paired with the S2 concession accepted in m14 (S2 benefits Northwind).

S1_incident_reporting.quote: Incidents involving fire, injury, evacuation, or property damage must be reported within 24 hours of discovery; other thermal incidents must be reported within five business days. Affected customers must be notified within 48 hours for urgent incidents and within five business days for other reportable incidents.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: A failure rate above 5% requires a regulator-reviewed corrective-action plan and retesting; it does not by itself prohibit sale or require withdrawal. Customers who buy a model must receive its per-model test results and any relevant safety information in an accessible form; this does not require general-public publication of individual-company results.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: All new home battery units must include a remote emergency shut-off capability no later than 12 months after adoption. Manufacturers must retrofit installed units that lack this capability within six years after adoption, where technically feasible... Any unit that cannot be safely retrofitted must be identified to its owner and the relevant regulator, with an alternative safe decommissioning or replacement plan.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: All new home battery units must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption. The suppression system must be appropriate to the battery chemistry and designed to reduce the risk of fire spread and harm to occupants and neighbours.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: When a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, the manufacturer must promptly notify the relevant regulator and provide the underlying incident-rate data and a corrective-action plan. A recall is mandatory when the regulator determines that a continuing unacceptable thermal risk cannot be adequately controlled by other measures.

document.section_notes: The final S2 keeps the 5% failure benchmark but removes any sales stop, so a model above it can keep being sold under a corrective-action plan, which protects Northwind's Hearth 10. S5 replaces the 8-per-100k recall trigger with regulator discretion and an open corrective-action alternative, so no numeric recall is mandatory, which protects Halcyon's Ember 8. S3 (six-year retrofit) and S4 (36-month suppression) sit at the edges of the acceptable ranges, favouring Northwind and Halcyon respectively.
